paths.description: Bare-origin 404 error archetype; represents the only route discoverable without an opaque Drive resource identifier. Not covered: arbitrary user-content file URLs, because none was supplied or discoverable from this endpoint.

findings.summary: The 404 response gives no path to recover or locate the intended resource.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot and DOM show a clear 404 message, but the only link is an unlabeled wrapper around the Google logo pointing to google.com; there is no retry, back, help, or Drive recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a descriptive recovery area with a real heading and actions to return to Drive, retry, check the URL, or request access as appropriate.

findings.summary: The error surface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, computed html background remained rgb(255,255,255), text rgb(34,34,34), and color-scheme was normal; dark screenshot matches light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use system colors or light-dark() for background, text, and error artwork.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference does not increase secondary-text contrast.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-contrast: more, 15px ins text remained rgb(119,119,119) on white, the same as default.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a prefers-contrast: more rule or system colors to strengthen secondary text and preserve distinctions.

findings.summary: Secondary error text narrowly misses normal-text contrast.
findings.evidence: #777 on #fff computes to about 4.48:1 at 15px for “That’s an error” and “That’s all we know,” below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken secondary text to at least #767676 on white, with a small safety margin such as #6b6b6b.

findings.summary: The error page has no heading structure.
findings.evidence: DOM/evaluate probe found h1Count 0; “404.” is a b element inside a paragraph. A main landmark exists and focus is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the error summary a concise h1 and retain the explanation and recovery controls beneath it.

findings.summary: The response omits the HTML doctype.
findings.evidence: Raw response starts with <html lang="en" dir=ltr>; document.doctype is null.
findings.suggestedFix: Begin the response with <!doctype html> to guarantee standards mode.

findings.summary: Transport and browser-defense policy is incomplete on the 404 response.
findings.evidence: Header/cookie probes show HTTPS, CSP, Trusted Types and nosniff, but no HSTS, Referrer-Policy, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, and NID is set without Secure with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the parent security-header baseline consistently: HSTS, an explicit referrer policy, frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, and Secure on SameSite=None cookies.

findings.summary: The bare error response sets a long-lived identifier cookie without an evident page need.
findings.evidence: Cookie probe recorded NID on .google.com with a 183-day expiry on this static 404; tracker probe found no known tracker requests and only www.google.com image requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid setting personalization/identifier cookies on anonymous error responses unless strictly necessary; document the purpose and scope if retained.

findings.summary: The failure state is legible but not actionable.
findings.evidence: Main request returns HTTP 404 and the visible response has no retry, Drive-home, support, or access-recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide context-appropriate recovery controls and preserve enough request context to help users correct the URL or regain access.

taskList.title: Make the 404 state actionable with semantic recovery controls
Apply complete security headers and cookie attributes to error responses
